name: Neural Voxel Renderer (NVR)
text:
# Neural Voxel Renderer (NVR)
Also called: NVR+
## Overview
The Neural Voxel Renderer (NVR) synthesizes realistic images from 3D [voxel representations](#19656-voxel-representation.md) while enabling explicit editing of illumination, object geometry, and appearance [S1]. It extends standard voxel rendering by incorporating a [splatting](#23-splatting.md) network and a neural re-rendering network to preserve high-frequency textures and complex lighting that analytical methods typically smooth out [S1].
## How it works
**Inputs and Outputs:**
*   **Input:** A 3D voxel grid representing the object's geometry and appearance, along with parameters defining the camera view and light source position or environment map [S1].
*   **Output:** A synthesized 2D image of the object from the target viewpoint [S1].
**Data Structures:**
*   **Voxel Grid:** The object is represented as a voxel volume [S1]. The standard initial resolution is $100^3$ [S1]. The scene volume is defined as $V \in 128^3 \times 4$ [S1].
*   **Lighting Input:** Can be simple light coordinates or a $32 \times 32$ environment map for realism [S1].
**Algorithm Steps:**
The rendering process, particularly in the NVR+ variant, follows these steps [S1][S2, unofficial]:
1.  **Splatting:** A splatting network synthesizes images by splitting colored voxel centers in the target view [S2, unofficial].
2.  **Feature Encoding:** The preliminary image and an NVR feature vector (including light position or a latent code from the environment map) are passed into a 2D convolutional encoder [S2, unofficial].
3.  **Neural Re-rendering:** The encoded features are processed by a neural re-rendering network to refine the image, adding high-frequency details, shadows, and specular highlights [S1][S2, unofficial].
4.  **Output Generation:** The network produces the final output image [S2, unofficial].
**Parameters:**
*   **Voxel Resolution:** The default initial resolution is $100^3$ [S1]. Performance decreases gracefully at $25^3$ but still produces plausible outputs [S1]. Lower resolutions are handled via [nearest-neighbor interpolation](#5891-nearest-neighbor-interpolation.md) during evaluation [S1].
*   **Environment Map:** For the realism variant, the environment map resolution is $32 \times 32$ [S1]. It is processed by convolutional layers to extract a latent code supplied to the NVR+ network [S1].
*   **Scene Volume:** $V \in 128^3 \times 4$ [S1].
**Edge Cases and Pitfalls:**
*   **Resolution Artifacts:** Significant loss of fine texture detail occurs at low resolutions ($25^3$) compared to the $100^3$ baseline [S1].
*   **Lighting Complexity:** Simple light coordinates may not capture complex environment shading as effectively as the environment map latent code approach [S1].
## Operating characteristics
*   **Time and Memory Complexity:** Not given in the sources.
*   **Performance:** The method produces plausible outputs even at low voxel resolutions ($25^3$) [S1].
*   **Quality:** NVR captures color and structure but smooths fine texture details [S1]. NVR+ accurately renders geometry and texture, synthesizing shadows, specular reflections, and highlights [S1].
*   **Comparison:** Compared to Image Translation models (which suffer from [GAN](#14030-adversarial-training-gan.md) artifacts and poor shadow estimation) and [Deep Shading](#15515-textured-mesh-refinement.md) models (which face similar limitations despite using mesh representations), NVR+ offers superior texture and lighting fidelity [S1].
*   **Usage:** The model was trained on the ShapeNet chair category and tested on real-world objects from the Pix3D and Ikea datasets (sofas, tables, etc.), demonstrating generalization to unseen categories [S1].
## Background
The Neural Voxel Renderer is a framework that synthesizes realistic images given object voxels as input, providing editing functionalities for illumination, object geometry, and appearance [S1]. It builds on the principles of [differentiable rendering](#16276-differentiable-rendering.md) and neural image synthesis [S1]. The NVR+ variant specifically incorporates a re-rendering module to handle complex textures and lighting effects like shadows and specularities, which the base splatting process alone cannot fully resolve [S1].
## Sources
[S1] Neural Voxel Renderer: Learning an Accurate and Controllable Rendering Tool, https://doi.org/10.1109/cvpr42600.2020.00546, fetched 2026-10-26
[S2] Neural Rendering and Its Hardware Acceleration: A Review, https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2402.00028, fetched 2026-10-26 (unofficial)
